pair.title: Nibe Live
pair.not_connected: Not connected to your heat pump

detect.title: Detecting features
detect.intro: Connecting to your heat pump and watching which values change. This takes about half a minute.
detect.failed: Can't read from your heat pump
detect.no_data: Something answers at this address, but it returns no NIBE data. Check the IP is your heat pump's own and that Modbus TCP is on (menu 7.5.9).

features.title: Select features
features.intro: Choose what to show. We've ticked what your heat pump reported.
features.insights_note: Disabling a feature removes its capabilities, including their Insights history.

evidence.unsupported: not supported by your heat pump

discover.searching: Searching your network for Nibe heat pumps…
discover.none_found: No heat pump found automatically. Check that Modbus TCP is enabled on your heat pump (menu 7.5.9) or enter its IP address below.
discover.title: Find your heat pump
discover.confirm: Found your heat pump — tap to confirm

devices.title: Add devices
devices.intro: Your heat pump does several jobs. Each gets its own device in Homey. We ticked the ones with live data.
devices.select_one: Select at least one device to add.
devices.main_desc: Overview: outdoor temperature, operating priority and mode, plus diagnostics and statistics
devices.analytics_desc: Helps the app author see which models and features are actually used, and where setup fails. No personal data, no readings from your home, no network details. You can change this later under app settings.

sources.prompt: More than one sensor can report this. Pick the one that should regulate:

tank.title: Hot water tank
tank.hint: Needed for the hot water estimate. Pick your tank's series, like VPB. The lining doesn't matter.
tank.inlet_hint: 10 °C is the usual figure; a little lower in winter, higher in summer.

setup.title: Device setup
setup.intro: Set up the functions you selected.
setup.heating_intro: Smart mode, indoor temperature and thermostat zone.
setup.nibe: Use your heat pump’s own temperature sensor
setup.homey: Use your own Homey temperature sensors
setup.promise: Let your rooms guide the heating
setup.promise_desc: Use the temperature sensors you already have in Homey. Choose one room, or average several for a temperature that represents your home. Your heat pump keeps its thermostat and Smart Price Adaption.
setup.picker_intro: Find sensors by name, room, device type or app. Choose one or combine several.
setup.review_intro: Each selected sensor has equal influence.
setup.pending_hint: Add your devices first, then open Heating → Repair to finish the setup. Leave your current NIBE sensor in control until then. No temperatures are sent during pairing.
setup.pump_intro: Check these settings on your heat pump, then verify here.
setup.pump_enable: Let your heat pump take a room temperature from Homey. Turn on external room sensor BT50 in menu 7.5.9.2.
setup.pump_zone: Assign BT50 to your heating zone in room sensor / zone settings (1.3.3 / 1.3.4).
setup.pump_control: Tell your heat pump to heat by BT50. Remove the sensor it used before if you're replacing it.
setup.zone_confirm: I have selected BT50 to control the intended zone.
setup.verified: Your heat pump received the temperature at BT50.
setup.active_note: Temperature updates continue in the background. To stop them, use Heating Setup to return to your NIBE sensor first.
setup.handover_hint: On your heat pump, select your original sensor to control the zone and disable external BT50. The current feed continues until you verify here.
setup.handover_confirm: My NIBE sensor is controlling the zone again.
setup.no_nibe_sources: No live NIBE source choices were detected. The current/default source will be kept.
setup.thermostat_zone_title: Which zone should the thermostat set?
setup.thermostat_zone_intro: Your heat pump has more than one zone. Choose the zone that controls the heating: on your heat pump, that zone’s room sensor is set to control (menu 1.3.3).
setup.analytics_benefit: Nibe Live is built by one developer with one heat pump. Sharing how the app works with yours helps uncover compatibility issues, improve setup and focus development on the features you use.
setup.analytics_details: Includes your heat pump model, app features used and technical events such as setup failures and connection problems. Temperature readings, device names and Flow names are never included.
setup.analytics_optional: Optional. Turn it off anytime in device settings → Privacy.
setup.request_timeout: Homey did not respond. Please try again.
setup.source_intro: Choose which sensor supplies the indoor temperature used to control your heating.
setup.source_homey_desc: Use one sensor or average several rooms. Your heat pump stays in control.
setup.feed_short: Verification starts regular temperature updates, which continue after you close Repair.
setup.feed_recovery: If Homey or a sensor stops reporting, BT50 can raise an alarm. Switch back to your NIBE sensor and turn off external BT50 on your heat pump.
setup.zone_detail: Menus 1.3.3 / 1.3.4 · Assign BT50 to the zone you want to heat.
setup.control_detail: Replace the previous controlling sensor if needed.
setup.success_description: Your heat pump is now receiving temperatures from your Homey sensors.

smart.title: Smart mode
smart.section_heating: Who moves heating to cheaper hours.
smart.section_hotwater: Who moves hot water to cheaper hours.
smart.intro: Pick one. Only one planner can run at a time.
smart.choose_on_desc_heating: Learns your house, then heats a little more before expensive hours and a little less during them.
smart.choose_on_desc_hotwater: Learns when your household uses hot water, then heats the tank in the cheapest hours.
smart.choose_spa_desc: NIBE's own. It runs in your heat pump and gets prices through myUplink.
smart.choose_off_desc_hotwater: Hot water follows your heat pump's own settings.
smart.success_description: Comfort range, Away and status are on the Heating device. The thermostat sets the comfort temperature.
smart.spa_note: Autopilot turns off Smart price adaption for heating.
smart.indoor_missing: Set up the indoor temperature under Heating first.
smart.outdoor_forecast: Weather forecast. A sensor in the shade is more accurate.
smart.prices_fixed: Fixed price: nothing to shift. Set dynamic prices in Homey Energy.
smart.room_control_on: This is on in your heat pump. Turn it off, or it will undo what Autopilot does.
smart.room_control_unknown: Couldn't be read. Keep it off.
smart.bt1: Let Autopilot send the outdoor temperature (BT1)
smart.bt1_detail: On your heat pump, menu 7.5.9.2. Turn on external BT1.
smart.verify_intro: Autopilot checks that your heat pump takes its outdoor temperature.
smart.return_reminder: On your heat pump, turn off external BT1 in menu 7.5.9.2.
smart.outdoor_intro: Pick a sensor in the shade, or use the forecast.
smart.steer_intro: Pick one. Only one planner can run at a time.
smart.pump_intro: What your heat pump needs for your choices.
smart.room_control_optional: Optional. On lets your heat pump correct by room temperature. Turn it off before choosing Autopilot.
smart.pump_confirm: These are set on your heat pump
smart.row_cheaper: Heats more when power is cheap, less when it's expensive
smart.row_learns: Learns how your house holds heat
smart.cmp_note: Smart price adaption is NIBE's own: it runs in your heat pump and gets prices through myUplink.
smart.exp_learning_sub: At least 5 days. Nothing changes yet.
smart.exp_acting_sub: Heat moves around price peaks, within your Comfort range.
smart.ctl_away_sub: A lower temperature while you're out
smart.ctl_off_sub: Your heat pump takes over again
smart.section_pool: Who moves pool heating to cheaper hours.
smart.section_cooling: Who moves cooling to cheaper hours.
smart.choose_on_desc_pool: Will heat the pool in cheap and solar hours, within a band you set.
smart.choose_on_desc_cooling: Will pre-cool before price peaks and on solar surplus.
smart.choose_off_desc_pool: The pool follows your heat pump's own settings.
smart.choose_off_desc_cooling: Cooling follows your heat pump's own settings.
smart.hw_intro: A few things before Autopilot takes over hot water.
smart.hw_tank_intro: Autopilot plans in litres, so it needs your tank's size. Pick it once.
smart.hw_flows: Flows that turn on More hot water
smart.hw_flows_none: None. Only Autopilot will start charges.
smart.hw_flows_found: They'll start charges Autopilot didn't plan. Turn them off, or keep them for notifications.
smart.hw_flows_unknown: Your Flows couldn't be read. Turn off any that switch on More hot water on a schedule.
smart.hw_household_intro: Autopilot is still learning (__days__ days so far). Tell it a bit about your home so it can start well.
smart.hw_household_intro_unknown: Autopilot is still learning. Tell it a bit about your home so it can start well.
smart.hw_free: On a day off, when do you use the most hot water?
smart.household_invalid: Choose how many people live there and a shower time.
smart.hw_daytype_calendar: Today: __type__. Saturday and Sunday are days off. Holiday or working from home? Change it on the Main device, or let a Flow follow your calendar.
smart.hw_daytype_set: Today: __type__, set on the Main device or by a Flow. It holds until changed.
smart.hw_reserve_hint: The least hot water Autopilot lets the tank drop to. A bigger cushion means the odd charge at a pricier hour.
smart.hw_reserve_invalid: Pick how much hot water to always keep.
smart.solar_intro: When your home is selling solar power, the tank can take it instead.
smart.solar_scanning: Looking for energy meters in your home…
smart.solar_meter_pick: Several found. Pick the one for your whole home.
smart.solar_evidence: In recent weeks you sent up to __kw__ kW to the grid on sunny hours.
smart.solar_evidence_plain: Your meter sends power to the grid on sunny hours.
smart.solar_live_hint: Hot water charges while your home exports power.
smart.solar_forecast_hint: Skips a night charge when sun is forecast, and pauses itself if the forecast keeps missing. Leave it off if a battery or car charger uses your solar first.
smart.solar_no_meter_found: Found your solar panels, but no electricity meter that measures what you sell, like a P1 reader. Add it to Homey Energy, then come back here.
smart.solar_need_meter: Solar heating needs an electricity meter that measures what you sell, like a P1 reader. Add it to Homey Energy, then come back here.
smart.hw_reserve_20: 20 L, a rinse or the dishes
smart.mode_note: Live steers your heat pump. Simulated plans everything and shows what it would do, while your heat pump stays as it is.
smart.indoor_intro: Autopilot keeps it at your thermostat's setting.
smart.indoor_homey_desc: One sensor, or the average of several rooms. Autopilot regulates on them, your heat pump doesn't.
smart.indoor_note: Autopilot steers your heat pump through the outdoor temperature (BT1), so room-sensor control on your heat pump stays off.
smart.indoor_source_prompt: More than one sensor can report this. Pick the one Autopilot reads:
smart.indoor_bt50_note: Your Homey sensors keep going to your heat pump as BT50, so it reports no sensor fault. With room-sensor control off, it only shows them. Autopilot does the regulating.
smart.success_indoor: indoors now · Autopilot steers it to __target__ °C

changes.count_detail: What you picked from your heat pump
changes.autopilot_simulated: Autopilot, simulated: it plans and shows, your heat pump stays as it is
changes.autopilot_uses: Autopilot acts on these, so they stay on while it runs
changes.spa_back: Back, now that Autopilot is off

gateway.title: Gateway connection
gateway.hint: Pick how your gateway numbers NIBE register 40025. Not sure? Ask whoever set it up.
gateway.invalid: Choose a gateway, a port from 1–65535 and a Modbus ID from 1–247.
gateway.detect_intro: Checking the values your heat pump reports. Depending on the gateway, this can take several minutes.

firmware.title: Update your heat pump first
firmware.intro: Many features need recent software on your heat pump. Older versions miss readings the app relies on and can even report wrong energy figures.
firmware.online_body: When an update is waiting, approve it in the myUplink app — or on your heat pump's display: swipe to the product overview and tap Update.
firmware.usb_body: Download the latest software from myuplink.com and put it on a USB stick. Insert it in the port above the display and open menu 8.1.
firmware.f_title: Via myUplink or a USB stick
firmware.f_body: The steps differ between models — your heat pump's manual shows how.
firmware.note: Takes a few minutes. Your settings are kept.

hotwater.cal_waiting: Charge cycles recorded so far: __CYCLES__. Two that heat the tank differently are needed before a size can be worked out.

connection.unreachable: Can't reach your heat pump at __host__. Check that it's on the network and that its IP address hasn't changed.

connection.searching: Can't reach your heat pump at __host__. Searching the network for it…
connection.moved: Nibe Live: your heat pump moved from __from__ to __to__. Its Homey devices have been updated.
connection.address_in_use: Another paired heat pump already uses __host__.
